messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] creating a genome like hg19
parts:
Hi Ranjan,

genome='hg18' is truly metadata. It is not going to pull any data from any server.

You can use any bed file formatted on the lines of UCSC ( atleast bed12) could be used. For further details about the UCSC bed you may refer to this previous post on this forum.

You may also try creating a gene.obj if you have a gff3 or gtf file. You would need to fiddle with bioconductor (GenomicFeatures) if you start with gff3 or gtf file. The same post referred above has further details on this.


Regards,
Kalyan


On 28 March 2014 23:35, <pran...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

 I have bismark output for a plant genome. How do I create a genome that I can input in following code (ucsc browser doesnot have data for genome of my interest)?

eg. myobj=read( file.list, sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),assembly="hg18",treatment=c(1,1,0,0))


Is hg18 in the above code being used to pull data from somewhere or is it just metadata that gets stored in the created object?


Also, can I just create a bed file and use with the genome of my interest?gene.obj=read.transcript.features(system.file("extdata", "refseq.hg18.bed.txt", package = "methylKit"))

Thanks
Ranjan
